question.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}17 & -8 \\ -8 & 17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}17-\lambda  & -8 \\ -8 & 17-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (17-\lambda )(17-\lambda )-64 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-34\lambda +289-64 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-34\lambda +225 & =0 \\ (\lambda -9)(\lambda -25) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =25,\,9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{25}=5 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{9}=3\end{aligned}
$$
